prize_parts.citation: For foundational contributions to the theory of nominal rigidities, staggered price and wage setting, and policy rules, which established the framework of modern monetary policy analysis.

statement.case_for: In the openings I ranked B015 first and B001 third. I now prefer B001 as the single-part configuration. It is the one candidate that nearly every colleague placed in their top three or five, and the reason is substantive, not just numerical. Calvo supplied the tractable time-dependent pricing device, Taylor supplied staggered contracts and the policy rule, and Woodford supplied the integrated microfounded and welfare-based framework. Each contribution is separable and has been used for decades in theory and practice. The foundational work is 30 to 40 years old, so there is no timing risk. The usual test for a prize is whether an idea changed how a field reasons. This one meets it, because it changed how central banks describe, evaluate and communicate policy. As a contract theorist I also value that the three contributions can be identified in specific papers and not only in a general literature. That makes the three-name attribution defensible even though the field is crowded.
statement.case_against: Credit in B001 is diffuse. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets have strong claims, particularly on estimation and DSGE quantification. Any trio is therefore contestable, and a cap of three forces exclusions that a reasonable committee could dispute. The empirical record is also mixed. The Phillips-curve fit and the handling of heterogeneity have been questioned after 2008 and after the 2021 inflation. Earlier macro prizes (Lucas, Kydland-Prescott, Sargent-Sims) narrow the unclaimed space. If the Committee cannot settle attribution, B006 has the cleaner trio and B015 has the cleanest paper-level attribution.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B001 first. He sees Calvo, Taylor and Woodford as the most defensible three. He notes that Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are major contributors to estimation, and that the post-2021 inflation episode tested the framework without breaking it.
responses.response: I agree on the core trio, and it is why I moved B001 up. I would qualify the claim that the framework survived the inflation test. The evidence is mixed, and I would not treat it as validation. What supports the award is the originating ideas, which are the pricing device, the contract structure and the policy-rule framework. These stand apart from how well the estimated DSGE descendants forecast. That framing also answers the estimation-side claimants. Their work extends and quantifies the ideas but does not originate them, and I would keep that distinction in the citation.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B002 first. He argues that Kiyotaki-Moore's collateral-constraint mechanism is a foundational, clean two-person contribution. He also notes that its empirical identification is more mixed than its theoretical influence suggests.
responses.response: I accept that B002 has the cleanest attribution of the macro candidates. I also agree that Kiyotaki-Moore is a real mechanism, not a fashion. My reservation is the one you raised. The mechanism's influence runs mainly through calibrated models and does not rest on identified evidence. It also sits close to the 2022 financial-crisis recognition. B001 has a longer record of direct institutional use, so I put it ahead. I would not oppose B002 as an alternative, and I would not count its two-name attribution as a point against it.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B006 first. He says it gives a unified formal and empirical framework in which government is endogenous. He acknowledges that the 2024 institutions prize may reduce appetite and that the cross-country constitutional evidence is weaker than the theory.
responses.response: I agree on the scientific case, and B006 was my second choice. The concern about the 2024 prize is not decisive for me, since the approach and the questions differ. My reservation is about identification. The constitutional-effects results rest on cross-country variation, which is weaker evidence than the originating-idea contributions in B001. I would treat B006 as a serious alternative. I would not call it a weaker case on attribution, since the Persson-Tabellini-Besley trio is arguably cleaner than B001.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B015 second. He argues that structural demand estimation is the empirical backbone of modern IO, that the area has not been recognised since Tirole in 2014, and that Bresnahan's claim relative to Levinsohn is a close call.
responses.response: This is the argument that led me to rank B015 first, and I still think the contribution is concrete and widely reused in antitrust and merger review. Only four members ranked it, so I cannot present it as a shared view. The Bresnahan question also remains open, since the three-name cap leaves out real contributors. I keep B015 as an alternative and not as my preferred part. A methods-and-practice award in IO has a clear case, but the broader support is for B001. I am not treating the support counts as scientific merit. My ordering rests on my own judgment of influence and attribution.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee would accept excluding Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets from a three-person prize, or would prefer a different trio.
How much the post-2008 and post-2021 empirical record should count against the New Keynesian framework, as opposed to its originating ideas.
Whether Bresnahan or Levinsohn would belong in a B015 trio, which determines how strong that alternative is.
I cannot independently verify citation or adoption claims from the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. I am an adjunct at Chicago Booth, and my profile records a long committee overlap with Hassler, Krusell, Ellingsen and Svensson. None of these is a connection to the proposed laureates. My co-authors are not on the shortlist, and my own field of corporate finance is not represented by the preferred part.
